sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Cricket Australia broadened its independent inquiry regarding ball-tampering to also examine the Ashes series played in 2017-18. This followed claims made in a book by a former player suggesting the whole team knew about the tampering during a tour to South Africa. While some former team members supported these claims, current and other past players denied them.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The renewed focus brings fresh attention to a major past cricket scandal. The governing body stated that the inquiry provides a safe environment for participants to share accounts, while ensuring no retroactive punishments will occur.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The independent forum will remain open for six weeks, inviting past players, support staff, and management to contribute. A full report containing recommendations will be published within thirty days after the board receives it.
